title: Bind the attempt to its budget reservation (RESERVED to ACTIVATED) on the production activation path
description:
MEASURED GAP, filed by governor-7211ec87 09:03Z on worker-40cfc767's step-1/2 measurement of task-a91e9fe2 (full evidence: comment-36fe35ff on that row, plus the probe below). Board search for an existing owner returned ZERO matches.

THE GAP: nothing in production ever moves a budget reservation from RESERVED to ACTIVATED, so settlement can never run.
- budget-reservation.ts:194 reserveForAdmission mints state:"RESERVED", attemptRef:null.
- budget-reservation.ts:227 activateReservation is the ONLY writer of state:"ACTIVATED" + attemptRef.
- budget-ledger-holds.ts:245 activateBudgetReservation has ZERO production callers — its sole caller is budget-transition-fixtures.ts:131, imported only by three .test.ts files.
- budget-settlement.ts:162 settleReservation refuses BUDGET_SETTLEMENT_NOT_ACTIVATED when state !== "ACTIVATED" || !isRef(attemptRef); :164 correlates measurements on r.run !== record.attemptRef, so a null attemptRef leaves no correlation key at all.
PROBE (run inside apps/daemon, deleted in the same command, absence verified): reserve ok=true state=RESERVED attemptRef=null; settle ok=false issues=BUDGET_SETTLEMENT_NOT_ACTIVATED.

WHY IT IS OPEN: task-e194c5f6 deliberately shipped the reservation leg only (its step-2 DECISION 1: the budget aggregate may appear exactly once in a legs commit — decision-ledger-legs.ts:105 refuses a duplicate aggregateId across legs — and activateReservation moves zero units, so the ACTIVATED transition was deferred). That deferral was recorded as costing nothing downstream. THAT PART IS MEASURED FALSE: activation-ingress-commit.ts:11-17 states settleBudgetReservation works "without ever requiring an ACTIVATED record", which contradicts budget-settlement.ts:162. e194c5f6's own DoD 2 named "reservation AND activation"; only the reservation shipped.

THE WORK: call activateBudgetReservation with the attempt's ref on the REAL activation/attempt path (never a fixture, never a seeded state). Resolve the duplicate-aggregateId constraint honestly — the budget aggregate already occupies a leg of the activation commit, so this most likely commits its OWN decision rather than riding that leg; measure which, and record why. Also CORRECT the false comment at activation-ingress-commit.ts:11-17 in the same commit — a comment asserting a downstream property that does not hold is how this gap survived a QA-approved row.

DOWNSTREAM: task-a91e9fe2 (settlement composition, CRITICAL) is blocked on this — wired at its measured seam (effect-terminal-ledger.ts recordTerminalEffect:204) every production settlement would refuse NOT_ACTIVATED, with DoD 2's COMPLETE and PARTIAL arms unreachable while the UNKNOWN arm passes green (that row's own plan risk 2). task-1b0a8477 (budgets/coverage reader) sits behind a91e9fe2.

SHARED-SEAM WARNING: apps/daemon/src/activation/ is hot — a91e9fe2 and 93e8aab3 both hold activation-budget-stage.ts this hour. Handshake edit order in #general and SHA256 shared files before AND after every suite run.
definitionOfDone: On the production activation/attempt path, a reservation minted RESERVED is transitioned to ACTIVATED with the attempt's own ref bound — proven by driving the real path (no fixture, no seeded state) and reading the durable record back through committed readers: state === "ACTIVATED" and attemptRef is the attempt's ref

settleReservation no longer refuses BUDGET_SETTLEMENT_NOT_ACTIVATED for a reservation produced by that path — demonstrated end-to-end, and the demonstration names the commit seam chosen (own decision vs shared leg) with the decision-ledger-legs.ts:105 duplicate-aggregateId constraint measured, not assumed
The false comment at activation-ingress-commit.ts:11-17 is corrected to state what production actually does
Refusals carry exact stable code AND refusing layer; a drill that breaks the binding (attemptRef left null, or the transition skipped) reddens named assertions
Explicit-pathspec commit; separate gate legs with counts verbatim; path-attributed baseline for foreign reds; peer-file SHA256 before AND after each run while the activation lane is hot
taskRails: Compose the existing primitives — activateBudgetReservation / activateReservation are landed and correct; do NOT reimplement the transition or edit the scheduler's arithmetic
No fixture-only proof: the accepted case must be constructed by driving the production activation path, per the rail that killed every seeded-state shortcut on this lane

The duplicate-aggregateId constraint is production-deliberate (decision-ledger-legs.ts:105) — satisfy it, never relax it; if the only honest answer is a second decision, take it and record the ordering/atomicity consequence
TDD; <=250 lines per production source touched; explicit-pathspec commits

implementationPlan.description: THE CORRELATION-IDENTITY FINDING — MEASURE, DISCLOSE, DO NOT PAPER OVER (this is the plan's most important non-obvious clause; the filing does not know about it). MEASURED: settlement's second gate compares each measurement's `r.run` against `record.attemptRef` (budget-settlement.ts:164; reconcile likewise :211). `r.run` is `measurement.providerRunRef`, and production fills it with a COMPOSITE built by the UNEXPORTED runRefOf (packages/runner/src/providers/telemetry/provider-usage-normalization.ts:61-64): `${provider}:${len(runRef)}:${runRef}:${len(attemptRef)}:${attemptRef}:${epoch}` — for this path `claude:{len}:{deriveDispatchAggregateId(...)}:{len}:{attemptId}:{leaseEpoch}` (assembled server-side at foundation-attempt-service.ts:159-163). So binding the BARE attemptId — which is what DoD 1 demands verbatim and what the field is named — clears NOT_ACTIVATED but will meet BUDGET_SETTLEMENT_UNCORRELATED_MEASUREMENT the moment REAL telemetry is fed in.
